title: Byte-gated crackme
subtitle: Four 1-in-256 gates, then a crash. Coverage guidance cracks it a byte at a time.
intro: Each gate compares one byte of the input. A blind fuzzer would need 2^32 tries; a coverage-guided fuzzer keeps every input that reaches a new gate and mutates from there, so it falls through in the low thousands. The last gate divides by zero -- the fault the fuzzer is hunting.

title: Shallow divide-by-zero
subtitle: One scramble, one bad divisor. Found fast, with or without coverage.
intro: No gates here: roughly one input in 256 scrambles to the divisor value that divides by zero. Fuzzing finds it quickly, which is the point of the contrast -- depth, not just the presence of a bug, is what makes coverage guidance matter.

title: Gate, then an out-of-bounds read
subtitle: A coverage gate guards an unchecked table index. The crash is a memory fault, not a divide.
intro: The high half of the input must equal 0x4242 before the code runs at all -- a gate coverage guidance falls through. Past it, the low half indexes a four-entry table with no bounds check, so a large index reads far out of range and the engine faults. Unlike the divide-by-zero targets, this crash is an out-of-bounds read: run it, then open the triage view to see how that fault is classified.
